clue.text: Doctor enables pair to get inextricably linked

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters of these two words, used as written

explanation.surface: A physician helps a couple become bound together for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person at the start of the sentence, but it is a verb meaning tamper with, telling you to rearrange the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that cannot be separated or pulled apart are bound together so tightly that untangling them is impossible.

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the letters that follow are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters of these words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A cook insists that a quince served on its own is still worth eating.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifteen letters is a long anagram; the apostrophe in 'isn't' is ignored, as punctuation always is in fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no consequence has no importance or worth, making it trivial and without any real value.

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside you, so one piece sits within another
in a down clue, standing up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a lass is a girl, especially in northern English and Scottish use
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A respectable young woman is holding a single thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' reads as honest or respectable, but in a down clue it tells you to write the whole thing upwards. LA(I)SS becomes SISAL when reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff natural fibre from an agave plant, used to make rope, twine and matting.

clue.text: Agent upset about most recent smear

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, and in a down clue tipping something over turns it upside down
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
the most recent one is the last one

explanation.surface: A disgruntled agent complains about the latest slur against a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smear' suggests slander given the agent, but here it is the physical sense of spreading something thickly. In a down clue, upset turns the agent bottom to top before it wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: To plaster is to spread or daub something thickly over a surface, just as to smear is.

blocks.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
the borders of an area are its sides or edges

explanation.surface: Someone makes their home on the frontier between two countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about living near a frontier, but 'on' and 'borders' are separate pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to have your home there, which is what it means to live in a place.

clue.text: Prepared lean crab and another crustacean

indicators.note: food that has been prepared has been chopped and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters as written

explanation.surface: A seafood platter of dressed crab with a second kind of shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another crustacean' works because the crab in the fodder is itself a crustacean.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnacles look like shellfish but are in fact crustaceans, related to crabs and shrimps, that cling to rocks and hulls.

clue.text: Still, in strange sense, showing indifference

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an odd order
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: still means not moving at all
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shows a curiously muted response, apparently unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like the adverb meaning nevertheless, but it is the adjective for not moving, and it sits inside the jumbled word rather than beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no emotion means being unmoved and detached, which is the same state as having no concern or interest.

clue.text: Note in favour of church is what keeps one down to earth

definitions.text: what keeps one down to earth

blocks.note: G is one of the musical notes A to G
to be for something is to favour it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Supporting the church is what keeps a person grounded and humble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down to earth' suggests modesty, but the definition is literal: the pull of gravity holds you to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The force of gravity, measured in units of g, is the pull that stops us floating away from the planet's surface.

indicators.note: without a leader means without the one at the front, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: rangers are the wardens who patrol forests and parks

explanation.surface: Park wardens with no one in charge drive people mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letter of RANGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuriate someone is to make them furious, which means to provoke their rage or temper.

clue.text: Plant, initially from Umbria, cultivated here shows impressive adaptability

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.clueFragment: from Umbria, cultivated here shows impressive adaptability
blocks.note: the first letter of each of the seven words

explanation.surface: A plant that originated in Italy thrives in our garden, proving it adapts well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially from Umbria' reads like 'originally from Umbria', but 'initially' takes the first letter of every following word, starting with 'from' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuchsia is a flowering shrub with drooping purple and red blooms, popular in gardens and hanging baskets.

clue.text: Knight to look fashionable with cut

blocks.note: a knight is addressed as Sir
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
what is fashionable is in

explanation.surface: A knight wants to appear stylish with a smart new haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' suggests a haircut, but it is a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirloin is a prime joint of beef taken from the loin, one of the butcher's best-known cuts of meat.

indicators.note: restyling gives something a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters as written

explanation.surface: A man called Glen experimented with a new curly hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: Corkscrews here are the spiral curls of hair, not the wine-opening tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringlets are long spiral curls of hair, so hair bearing ringlets has twisting corkscrew-shaped locks.

indicators.note: a thief takes the stolen goods into their keeping, so one piece ends up inside another

blocks.note: an aide is an assistant
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Should you put up with a helper who pinches a book?
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside AIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: If you cannot abide something you cannot bear or put up with it, so the verb means to endure.

clue.text: You and I imprisoned by queen in jug

indicators.note: a prisoner is held within walls, so one piece is shut inside another

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: Two people locked up by a queen end up in jug, slang for prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In jug' sounds like British slang for in jail, which fits the imprisonment, but the jug is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed pitcher, traditionally used to carry water for washing.

blocks.note: to rat on someone and to grass on them both mean to inform on them to the police
to plant a blow is to land it

explanation.surface: A rodent sows seeds across the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is British slang for informing to the police, a sense shared with rat; both clue words are verbs, not the rodent and the greenery they suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadows are open fields covered with grass, which is exactly what grassland consists of.

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so the first piece sits below the second

blocks.note: dome is slang for a person's head
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A fool backs the leaders behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for a person, but it is a twitch, and in a down answer it sits beneath the heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic matters belong to the home and family life rather than the public world, so they are personal ones.

clue.text: Animated dog caught by spirited government

blocks.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in the Disney cartoons
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
racy can mean lively or spirited

explanation.surface: A lively cartoon dog is seized by an energetic regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animated' reads as lively, but it means a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutocracy is rule by the wealthy, a form of state power in which the rich hold control.

indicators.note: a drill boring into something goes inside it, so one piece is buried in another

blocks.note: a plate is a dish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sample a dull meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like the adjective dull, but it is the verb drilling into: A goes inside PLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a fine palate has a discerning sense of flavour, so the word also means a person's taste.

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: embarrassed people go red, so more embarrassed is redder
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone is even more ashamed over a sport played in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests a sport, but it means animals hunted for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Red deer are hunted and stalked for sport and venison, so they count as wild quarry hunted for the table.

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
an alp is a high mountain peak
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stakes a claim to a mountain summit: it belongs to me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as the possessive 'belonging to me', but it is the noun for a place where coal is dug.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalpit is a pit from which coal is extracted, an underground excavation for fuel.

blocks.note: first meaning: a wild plant growing where it is not wanted
second meaning: slang for cannabis
third meaning: informal past tense for urinated, as in 'took a leak'

explanation.surface: A flowerpot holding a houseplant has sprung a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate meanings of one short word, the last two in slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for an unwanted wild plant, slang for cannabis, and a childish verb meaning passed water.

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
consumed food means ate it

explanation.surface: An academic gobbled up a present he had been given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gift' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb meaning to give.
explanation.definitionFit: To gift something is to give it away freely, which is what donating means, typically to a charity.

clue.text: Cut delicate fabric covering bottom of cushion

indicators.note: the bottom of a word written across is its end, so only the final letter is kept
a cover goes around and over something, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: lace is a fine openwork fabric
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Trim the dainty material that covers the underside of a cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the last letter of cushion, goes inside LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance a boil is to pierce it with a sharp blade, a small surgical incision.

definitions.note: an example of the answer: greed is one of the seven

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in place, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: the nine letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone eating at restaurants too often betrays a gluttonous appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like the comment on dining out, but the anagram indicator is 'out', and the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed, or avarice, is one of the seven deadly sins of Christian teaching, alongside pride, envy and gluttony.

blocks.note: the ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Anglers adore their specialist terminology.
explanation.walkthrough: LING is a crossword staple fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for the specialised vocabulary of a trade or group, the same thing as jargon.

clue.text: Plant taking top off pipe after time

indicators.note: removing the top of a word written across means losing its first letter
something that comes after another follows it, so the pieces are set one behind the other

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a pipe is a simple whistle

explanation.surface: A plant takes the lid off a pipe after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: WHISTLE loses its W and follows T.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is a prickly wild plant with purple flowers, the national emblem of Scotland.

clue.text: Cutting bit of wordplay by posh bloke

blocks.note: a pun is a joke that plays on words
gent is short for gentleman, a well-bred man

explanation.surface: An upper-class man delivers a sharp, witty remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of' does not select letters here; a bit of wordplay is a whole pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent remarks are sharply critical or caustic, just as cutting ones wound with their sharpness.

blocks.note: to doctor a drink is to lace it with something
rations are allotted portions of food

explanation.surface: A doctor's meals have been reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor's' looks like a possessive, but it is the verb doctors (laces) shortened to 'doctor's' with the apostrophe; 'Cuts' looks like a verb, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerations are deep, jagged wounds in the skin, the kind of injuries a sharp edge or blade leaves.
